title: Building Up a Freezer Stock of Bacteria
author: Katy M Monteith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vbce2iw

steps.title: Inoculate colony and grow overnight
steps.instruction: Select a single isolated colony from a growth‑media plate, inoculate it into LB broth, and incubate the culture overnight (≈16–18 h) as described in the plating protocol.

steps.title: Measure culture optical density (OD600)
steps.instruction: Using an absorbance microplate reader, measure the culture at 600 nm and confirm the optical density is between 0.6 and 0.8, indicating exponential growth.

steps.title: Add glycerol to achieve 20‑25% final
steps.instruction: Add sterile 100 % glycerol to the culture to reach a final glycerol concentration of 20‑25 % (e.g., add 2.5 mL glycerol to 10 mL culture). If the glycerol is difficult to pipette, trim ~4 mm off the tip of the pipette.

substeps.instruction: Add glycerol to reach 20‑25 % final concentration
Trim pipette tip ~4 mm if needed

steps.title: Mix and aliquot culture
steps.instruction: Vortex the glycerol‑culture mixture for at least 1 minute until thoroughly combined, then dispense the suspension into 100‑200 µL aliquots.

steps.title: Seal and store freezer stocks
steps.instruction: Place the aliquots into a sealed, labeled bag, put the bag into a sealed, labeled container, and store at –70 °C to –80 °C. Check viability periodically and replace stocks every 6‑12 months; when stocks run low, thaw an aliquot and repeat the plating and stock‑making steps.

substeps.instruction: Place aliquots in sealed, labeled bag
Place bag in sealed, labeled container
